## Overview

This document cleans and concatenates the raw PsychoPy output files from the Biosignals2 emotion-induction study, producing two analysis-ready CSVs:

- **`biosignals2_selfreport_ratings.csv`** — self-report ratings (valence, arousal, approach-avoidance, emotion label/intensity) in long format, with one row per experimental phase per participant.
- **`biosignals2_webcambiometrics.csv`** — webcam biometrics (heart rate, facial action units, gaze) sampled continuously throughout the session, with each row labelled by experimental phase.

### Experimental design

Participants watched positive and negative emotion-induction video blocks (order counterbalanced), separated by a rest/recovery period. Each block contained two videos. Self-report ratings were collected:

- Once before and once after a **baseline** fixation cross
- After each **emotion induction** block (post-induction)
- After each **recovery** fixation cross (post-recovery)
- After each individual video (stimulus-level ratings)

Conditions in the output are coded as:

| Condition label | Description |
|----|----|
| `baseline` | Resting fixation cross period |
| `negative_induction` | Negative emotion video block |
| `post_negative_induction_recovery` | Recovery fixation cross after negative block |
| `positive_induction` | Positive emotion video block |
| `post_positive_induction_recovery` | Recovery fixation cross after positive block |

The `baseline` row additionally carries `block_start_valence`/`block_start_arousal` (the pre-baseline state rating) alongside `block_end_valence`/`block_end_arousal` (the post-baseline rating), enabling trajectory analysis in downstream scripts.

### Experiment versions

Two versions of the PsychoPy task are handled in this pipeline:

- **v1 (pilot):** Valence collected on two alternating sliders (A then B, or B then A, counterbalanced). Columns: `momentary_valence_slider_A/B.response`, `stim_valence_slider_A/B.response`.
- **v2 (July update):** Single combined valence + arousal screen; one slider each. Columns: `momentary_valence_slider.response`, `stim_valence_slider.response`.

Row-type identifiers (e.g. `pre_baseline_ratings.momentary_arousal_slider.response`) are unchanged between versions. Valence extraction uses a triple coalesce (A → B → single) so both formats flow through the same pipeline. A `data_version` column in intermediate outputs records which format each participant used.

## 1. Packages & configuration

```{r packages}
library(tidyverse)
library(yaml)
library(knitr)
```

```{r}

find_project_root <- function() {
  start <- dirname(rstudioapi::getSourceEditorContext()$path)
  current <- normalizePath(start, winslash = "/", mustWork = TRUE)
  
  repeat {
    config_path <- file.path(current, "config.R")
    
    if (file.exists(config_path)) {
      return(current)
    }
    
    parent <- dirname(current)
    
    if (parent == current) {
      stop("Could not find config.R in this directory or any parent directory.")
    }
    
    current <- parent
  }
}

project_dir <- find_project_root()
config_path <- file.path(project_dir, "config.R")

source(config_path)

psychopy_data_dir <- PSYCHOPY_DATA_DIR
clean_data_dir    <- COMBINED_PSYCHO_DIR
```

## 2. Load raw data

Participant ID is extracted as everything before the first `_` in the filename (e.g. `n2026`, `p7259`). Each participant produces two CSVs — a task file and a biometrics file — which have different column schemas and are loaded separately.

```{r load-data}
csv_files <- list.files(psychopy_data_dir, pattern = "\\.csv$", full.names = TRUE)
if (length(csv_files) == 0) stop("No CSV files found in: ", psychopy_data_dir)

# Leave out test sessions: status "test" in analysis/participant_status.csv (e.g. 001 and
# 002, which pre-date the emotion label question). Matched on the exact ID before the first
# "_", so a timestamp containing "001" can't drop a real participant. Pilots and rejected
# participants are KEPT in the combined data — the QC reports need them, and the analysis
# scripts filter them out themselves.
analysis_dir <- if (basename(project_dir) == "analysis") project_dir else file.path(project_dir, "analysis")
PARTICIPANT_STATUS_PATH <- file.path(analysis_dir, "participant_status.csv")
source(file.path(analysis_dir, "participant_status.R"), local = TRUE)
file_pids    <- norm_participant_id(sub("_.*", "", basename(csv_files)))
dropped_test <- sort(unique(file_pids[file_pids %in% test_ids()]))
csv_files    <- csv_files[!file_pids %in% test_ids()]
if (length(dropped_test)) cat("Left out (test sessions):", paste(dropped_test, collapse = ", "), "\n")

# Split by file type — task and biometrics have different schemas
task_files       <- csv_files[!grepl("_biometrics\\.csv$", csv_files)]
biometrics_files <- csv_files[ grepl("_biometrics\\.csv$", csv_files)]

extract_pid <- function(path) tolower(sub("_.*", "", basename(path)))

# Read all files in a set as character first, then infer types after binding
# (avoids type-conflict errors when the same column differs across files)
load_csv_set <- function(files) {
  map_dfr(files, function(path) {
    df <- read_csv(path,
                   show_col_types = FALSE,
                   col_types      = cols(.default = col_character()),
                   name_repair    = "minimal",
                   locale         = locale(encoding = "UTF-8"))
    names(df)[1] <- gsub("^﻿", "", names(df)[1])  # strip BOM
    df$participant_id <- extract_pid(path)
    df
  }) |>
    type_convert(guess_integer = FALSE)
}

raw_task       <- load_csv_set(task_files)
raw_biometrics <- load_csv_set(biometrics_files)

cat("Task files loaded      :", length(task_files), "\n")
cat("Task participants      :", paste(sort(unique(raw_task$participant_id)),       collapse = ", "), "\n")
cat("Biometrics files loaded:", length(biometrics_files), "\n")
cat("Biometrics participants:", paste(sort(unique(raw_biometrics$participant_id)), collapse = ", "), "\n")
```

## 3. Helper functions

```{r helpers}
# Coalesce two numeric-like columns, suppressing conversion warnings
coalesce_val <- function(a, b) {
  coalesce(suppressWarnings(as.numeric(a)),
           suppressWarnings(as.numeric(b)))
}

# Triple coalesce: handles both v1 (A/B sliders) and v2 (single slider).
# For v1 participants, A or B will be non-NA and is returned.
# For v2 participants, A and B are always NA, so the single-slider column is used.
coalesce_val3 <- function(a, b, single) {
  coalesce(coalesce_val(a, b), suppressWarnings(as.numeric(single)))
}

# Records slider presentation order for v1 participants (NA for v2).
slider_order_flag <- function(a, b) {
  case_when(
    !is.na(suppressWarnings(as.numeric(a))) ~ "valence_first",
    !is.na(suppressWarnings(as.numeric(b))) ~ "valence_second",
    TRUE ~ NA_character_
  )
}

# Tag each participant with their experiment version
format_map <- raw_task |>
  group_by(participant_id) |>
  summarise(
    data_version = if_else(
      any(!is.na(suppressWarnings(as.numeric(`momentary_valence_slider_A.response`)))),
      "v1_pilot", "v2_jul"
    ),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

print(format_map)
```

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## 4. Extract PsychoPy event data

PsychoPy outputs a wide, sparse format where each row is a single loop iteration. Prefixed columns (e.g. `pre_baseline_ratings.*`) identify which routine a row belongs to; actual response values are in the top-level columns.

Valence is extracted with `coalesce_val3` to handle both task versions. Arousal column names are unchanged between versions.

### 4.1 Condition order

```{r cond-order}
cond_order <- raw_task |>
  filter(!is.na(conditionOrder) & conditionOrder != "") |>
  distinct(participant_id, conditionOrder)
```

### 4.2 Momentary ratings

One row per participant per timepoint. The `pre_baseline_ratings.*`, `post_baseline_ratings.*`, `post_emotion_induction_ratings.*`, and `post_emotion_recovery_ratings.*` prefixes identify which screen each row belongs to.

```{r momentary-ratings}
# Reusable extractor for momentary valence + arousal
extract_momentary <- function(data, indicator_col, prefix) {
  data |>
    filter(!is.na(.data[[indicator_col]])) |>
    transmute(
      participant_id,
      condition,
      "{prefix}_valence"       := coalesce_val3(
        `momentary_valence_slider_A.response`,
        `momentary_valence_slider_B.response`,
        `momentary_valence_slider.response`
      ),
      "{prefix}_valence_rt"    := coalesce_val3(
        `momentary_valence_slider_A.rt`,
        `momentary_valence_slider_B.rt`,
        `momentary_valence_slider.rt`
      ),
      "{prefix}_valence_slider_order" := slider_order_flag(
        `momentary_valence_slider_A.response`,
        `momentary_valence_slider_B.response`
      ),
      "{prefix}_arousal"       := as.numeric(`momentary_arousal_slider.response`),
      "{prefix}_arousal_rt"    := as.numeric(`momentary_arousal_slider.rt`)
    )
}

pre_bl   <- extract_momentary(raw_task,
              "pre_baseline_ratings.momentary_arousal_slider.response",   "prebl")
post_bl  <- extract_momentary(raw_task,
              "post_baseline_ratings.momentary_arousal_slider.response",  "postbl")
post_ind <- extract_momentary(raw_task,
              "post_emotion_induction_ratings.momentary_arousal_slider.response", "postind")
post_rec <- extract_momentary(raw_task,
              "post_emotion_recovery_ratings.momentary_arousal_slider.response",  "postrec")

# Baseline ratings don't have a meaningful condition; drop the column
pre_bl  <- select(pre_bl,  -condition)
post_bl <- select(post_bl, -condition)
```

### 4.3 Per-video stimulus ratings

`trigger_name` and `origional_video_id` appear on different rows in the raw output, so we build a lookup from the trigger rows and join it in.

```{r stim-ratings}
trigger_lookup <- raw_task |>
  filter(!is.na(trigger_name) & trigger_name != "",
         !is.na(stim_path)    & stim_path    != "") |>
  transmute(
    participant_id,
    video_id     = str_remove(basename(stim_path), "\\.[^.]+$"),
    trigger_name
  )

stim_ratings <- raw_task |>
  filter(!is.na(origional_video_id) & origional_video_id != "") |>
  transmute(
    participant_id,
    video_id  = origional_video_id,
    condition = case_when(
      str_starts(origional_video_id, "P") ~ "positive",
      str_starts(origional_video_id, "N") ~ "negative",
      TRUE ~ NA_character_
    ),
    stim_valence           = coalesce_val3(`stim_valence_slider_A.response`,
                                           `stim_valence_slider_B.response`,
                                           `stim_valence_slider.response`),
    stim_valence_rt        = coalesce_val3(`stim_valence_slider_A.rt`,
                                           `stim_valence_slider_B.rt`,
                                           `stim_valence_slider.rt`),
    stim_valence_slider_order = slider_order_flag(`stim_valence_slider_A.response`,
                                                  `stim_valence_slider_B.response`),
    stim_arousal           = as.numeric(`stim_arousal_slider.response`),
    stim_arousal_rt        = as.numeric(`stim_arousal_slider.rt`),
    stim_approach          = as.numeric(`stim_approach_slider.response`),
    stim_approach_rt       = as.numeric(`stim_approach_slider.rt`),
    stim_emotion_label        = emotionText.text,
    stim_emotion_intensity    = as.numeric(intensitySlider.response),
    stim_emotion_intensity_rt = as.numeric(intensitySlider.rt)
  ) |>
  left_join(trigger_lookup, by = c("participant_id", "video_id"))
```

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## 5. Join into one row per video and add manipulation checks

```{r join}
clean_data <- stim_ratings |>
  left_join(post_ind,   by = c("participant_id", "condition")) |>
  left_join(post_rec,   by = c("participant_id", "condition")) |>
  left_join(pre_bl,     by = "participant_id") |>
  left_join(post_bl,    by = "participant_id") |>
  left_join(cond_order, by = "participant_id") |>
  left_join(format_map, by = "participant_id") |>
  # Sort within participant so the first-presented condition appears first
  mutate(
    condition_rank = case_when(
      conditionOrder == "pos_first" & condition == "positive" ~ 1L,
      conditionOrder == "pos_first" & condition == "negative" ~ 2L,
      conditionOrder == "neg_first" & condition == "negative" ~ 1L,
      conditionOrder == "neg_first" & condition == "positive" ~ 2L,
      TRUE ~ NA_integer_
    )
  ) |>
  arrange(participant_id, condition_rank) |>
  select(-condition_rank) |>
  select(
    participant_id, data_version, conditionOrder, condition, video_id, trigger_name,
    stim_valence, stim_valence_rt, stim_valence_slider_order,
    stim_arousal, stim_arousal_rt,
    stim_approach, stim_approach_rt,
    stim_emotion_label, stim_emotion_intensity, stim_emotion_intensity_rt,
    postind_valence, postind_valence_rt, postind_valence_slider_order,
    postind_arousal, postind_arousal_rt,
    postrec_valence, postrec_valence_rt, postrec_valence_slider_order,
    postrec_arousal, postrec_arousal_rt,
    prebl_valence,  prebl_valence_rt,  prebl_valence_slider_order,
    prebl_arousal,  prebl_arousal_rt,
    postbl_valence, postbl_valence_rt, postbl_valence_slider_order,
    postbl_arousal, postbl_arousal_rt
  )

cat("Rows:", nrow(clean_data), "| Columns:", ncol(clean_data),
    "| Participants:", n_distinct(clean_data$participant_id), "\n")
```

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## 6. Label biometrics with experimental conditions

The biometrics stream is continuous. We label each sample by matching its timestamp to the event windows from the PsychoPy log.

**Clock alignment:** The biometrics `mono_time` column and PsychoPy's internal clock share the same monotonic source (confirmed via the per-session `_clocksync.json` file). They differ by a small per-session offset (≈ 0.6 s) representing the lag between biometrics recording start and experiment start. We estimate this offset per participant from `time_since_recording_start` (logged by PsychoPy on the biometrics clock) and apply it to convert PsychoPy event times to the biometrics clock.

```{r biometrics-label}
# Per-participant clock offset: biometrics mono_time − PsychoPy internal clock
# time_since_recording_start is logged by PsychoPy on the biometrics clock,
# so offset = time_since_recording_start − thisRow.t ≈ 0.6 s per session.
clock_offset <- raw_task |>
  filter(!is.na(time_since_recording_start), !is.na(`thisRow.t`)) |>
  mutate(offset = as.numeric(time_since_recording_start) - as.numeric(`thisRow.t`)) |>
  filter(abs(offset) < 10) |>  # drop anomalous rows (e.g. computer sleep/wake)
  group_by(participant_id) |>
  summarise(clock_offset_s = median(offset, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop")

# Build event time windows, converting PsychoPy times to biometrics clock
baseline_windows <- raw_task |>
  filter(!is.na(`baseline.started`)) |>
  left_join(clock_offset, by = "participant_id") |>
  transmute(participant_id, phase = "baseline", condition = NA_character_, video_id = NA_character_,
            start_bio = as.numeric(`baseline.started`) + clock_offset_s,
            end_bio   = as.numeric(`baseline.stopped`)  + clock_offset_s)

# Condition and video_id inferred from stim_path (the file path used to play the video),
# which is populated on stimulus timing rows. Note: origional_video_id is on the
# *rating* rows and identifies which specific stimulus the participant is rating —
# it is not available on the timing rows used here.
stimulus_windows <- raw_task |>
  filter(!is.na(`stimuli.started`), !is.na(stim_path), stim_path != "") |>
  left_join(clock_offset, by = "participant_id") |>
  transmute(participant_id, phase = "stimulus",
            condition = case_when(
              str_detect(stim_path, "/P|/p") ~ "positive",
              str_detect(stim_path, "/N|/n") ~ "negative",
              TRUE ~ NA_character_
            ),
            video_id  = str_remove(basename(stim_path), "\\.[^.]+$"),
            start_bio = as.numeric(`stimuli.started`) + clock_offset_s,
            end_bio   = as.numeric(`stimuli.stopped`)  + clock_offset_s)

recovery_windows <- raw_task |>
  filter(!is.na(`stim_recovery.started`)) |>
  left_join(clock_offset, by = "participant_id") |>
  transmute(participant_id, phase = "recovery", condition, video_id = NA_character_,
            start_bio = as.numeric(`stim_recovery.started`) + clock_offset_s,
            end_bio   = as.numeric(`stim_recovery.stopped`)  + clock_offset_s)

event_windows <- bind_rows(baseline_windows, stimulus_windows, recovery_windows) |>
  filter(!is.na(start_bio), !is.na(end_bio))

# Range-join: label each biometrics sample with the phase its mono_time falls in.
# Samples during rating screens / instructions have no matching window and are dropped.
raw_biometrics_labelled <- raw_biometrics |>
  mutate(mono_time = as.numeric(mono_time)) |>
  left_join(event_windows,
            by = join_by(participant_id, between(mono_time, start_bio, end_bio))) |>
  select(-start_bio, -end_bio) |>
  filter(!is.na(phase)) |>
  relocate(participant_id, phase, condition, video_id)

count(raw_biometrics_labelled, participant_id, phase, condition)
```

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## 7. Reshape to long format with unified condition labels

Both datasets are reshaped so that each row represents one experimental phase, using a consistent five-level `condition` factor.

```{r condition-labels}
cond_levels <- c("baseline", "negative_induction", "post_negative_induction_recovery",
                 "positive_induction", "post_positive_induction_recovery")

# --- Biometrics: merge phase + condition into single label ---
raw_biometrics_labelled <- raw_biometrics_labelled |>
  mutate(
    condition = factor(case_when(
      phase == "baseline"                            ~ "baseline",
      phase == "stimulus" & condition == "negative"  ~ "negative_induction",
      phase == "recovery" & condition == "negative"  ~ "post_negative_induction_recovery",
      phase == "stimulus" & condition == "positive"  ~ "positive_induction",
      phase == "recovery" & condition == "positive"  ~ "post_positive_induction_recovery",
      TRUE ~ NA_character_
    ), levels = cond_levels)
  ) |>
  select(-phase) |>
  relocate(participant_id, condition, video_id)

# --- Task data: pivot to long format ---
# block_start_valence/arousal = state rating at the START of the block (baseline only:
#   the pre-baseline rating). Used for trajectory analysis in downstream scripts.
# block_end_valence/arousal   = state rating at the END of each block.
# stim_* columns are NA for non-video phases.

na_stim <- list(
  stim_valence = NA_real_, stim_valence_rt = NA_real_,
  stim_arousal = NA_real_, stim_arousal_rt = NA_real_,
  stim_approach = NA_real_, stim_approach_rt = NA_real_,
  stim_emotion_label = NA_character_,
  stim_emotion_intensity = NA_real_, stim_emotion_intensity_rt = NA_real_
)

# Baseline: block_start = pre-baseline rating, block_end = post-baseline rating
baseline_rows <- clean_data |>
  distinct(participant_id, conditionOrder, data_version,
           prebl_valence, prebl_arousal, postbl_valence, postbl_arousal) |>
  transmute(participant_id, conditionOrder, data_version,
            condition = "baseline", video_id = NA_character_, trigger_name = NA_character_,
            block_start_valence = prebl_valence, block_start_arousal = prebl_arousal,
            block_end_valence = postbl_valence, block_end_arousal = postbl_arousal,
            !!!na_stim)

negative_rows <- clean_data |>
  filter(condition == "negative") |>
  transmute(participant_id, conditionOrder, data_version,
            condition = "negative_induction", video_id, trigger_name,
            block_start_valence = NA_real_, block_start_arousal = NA_real_,
            block_end_valence = postind_valence, block_end_arousal = postind_arousal,
            stim_valence, stim_valence_rt, stim_arousal, stim_arousal_rt,
            stim_approach, stim_approach_rt,
            stim_emotion_label, stim_emotion_intensity, stim_emotion_intensity_rt)

post_neg_rows <- clean_data |>
  filter(condition == "negative") |>
  distinct(participant_id, conditionOrder, data_version, postrec_valence, postrec_arousal) |>
  transmute(participant_id, conditionOrder, data_version,
            condition = "post_negative_induction_recovery",
            video_id = NA_character_, trigger_name = NA_character_,
            block_start_valence = NA_real_, block_start_arousal = NA_real_,
            block_end_valence = postrec_valence, block_end_arousal = postrec_arousal,
            !!!na_stim)

positive_rows <- clean_data |>
  filter(condition == "positive") |>
  transmute(participant_id, conditionOrder, data_version,
            condition = "positive_induction", video_id, trigger_name,
            block_start_valence = NA_real_, block_start_arousal = NA_real_,
            block_end_valence = postind_valence, block_end_arousal = postind_arousal,
            stim_valence, stim_valence_rt, stim_arousal, stim_arousal_rt,
            stim_approach, stim_approach_rt,
            stim_emotion_label, stim_emotion_intensity, stim_emotion_intensity_rt)

post_pos_rows <- clean_data |>
  filter(condition == "positive") |>
  distinct(participant_id, conditionOrder, data_version, postrec_valence, postrec_arousal) |>
  transmute(participant_id, conditionOrder, data_version,
            condition = "post_positive_induction_recovery",
            video_id = NA_character_, trigger_name = NA_character_,
            block_start_valence = NA_real_, block_start_arousal = NA_real_,
            block_end_valence = postrec_valence, block_end_arousal = postrec_arousal,
            !!!na_stim)

clean_data_long <- bind_rows(baseline_rows, negative_rows, post_neg_rows,
                             positive_rows, post_pos_rows) |>
  mutate(condition = factor(condition, levels = cond_levels)) |>
  relocate(participant_id, condition, video_id) |>
  arrange(participant_id, condition)

cat("Task rows by condition:\n")
count(clean_data_long, condition) |> print()
```

## 8. Quality checks

### 8.1 Missing data

```{r na-check}
clean_data_long |>
  summarise(across(everything(), ~ sum(is.na(.)))) |>
  pivot_longer(everything(), names_to = "column", values_to = "n_missing") |>
  filter(n_missing > 0) |>
  arrange(desc(n_missing)) |>
  kable(caption = "Missing values in clean_data_long")
```

### 8.2 Sanity check: mean ratings by condition and version

```{r sanity-check}
clean_data_long |>
  group_by(data_version, condition) |>
  summarise(
    n                  = n(),
    mean_block_valence = mean(block_end_valence, na.rm = TRUE),
    mean_block_arousal = mean(block_end_arousal, na.rm = TRUE),
    mean_stim_valence  = mean(stim_valence,      na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  kable(digits = 2, caption = "Mean ratings by condition and experiment version")
```

## 9. Save

```{r save}
dir.create(clean_data_dir, showWarnings = FALSE, recursive = TRUE)

# Drop internal bookkeeping columns before saving
clean_data_long <- select(clean_data_long, -data_version)

write_csv(clean_data_long,          file.path(clean_data_dir, "biosignals2_selfreport_ratings.csv"))
write_csv(raw_biometrics_labelled,  file.path(clean_data_dir, "biosignals2_webcambiometrics.csv"))

cat("Saved to:", clean_data_dir, "\n")
cat("  biosignals2_selfreport_ratings.csv —", nrow(clean_data_long), "rows\n")
cat("  biosignals2_webcambiometrics.csv   —", nrow(raw_biometrics_labelled), "rows\n")
```
